title: Goldbach numbers in intervals of length 2 log² x under the Riemann hypothesis
description:
Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we prove that for every x ≥ 4 the interval (x, x + 2 log² x] contains an even integer that is a sum of two primes. The previous best constant was 123, due to Chirre and Hagen. The improvement comes from three changes to the classical Selberg-integral argument. We pair intervals of relative length. We use a positive-definite weight on the logarithmic scale whose width grows like √(log x). And we evaluate the resulting zero sums exactly by the Weil explicit formula, which also makes the prime-power contribution negligible. The constant 2 is the limit of the method, and we compare it heuristically with Goldston's deduction, which reaches the same constant from mean-square bounds of the same size.

This archive contains the paper (LaTeX and PDF), the interval-arithmetic checks of every numerical constant in the proof, floating-point cross-checks, and a conditional Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of most of the deduction.

Status: unreviewed preprint, prepared largely with the AI model Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction. The result is conditional on the Riemann hypothesis.
